candidates.comment: Thanks for the detailed report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344726 already tracks this verifier SIGILL and the missing signal/stderr diagnostics. Your Lima/Ubuntu reproduction, strace confirmation, and unsuccessful process-local overrides add useful evidence; signature verification should remain enabled, and the proposed .NET connection still needs confirmation.

Thanks for the report. This matches the reasoning-item ID failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/309861, including failures after Auto model selection and retries that cannot recover the conversation. This report adds an occurrence on Windows with VS Code 1.145.1 after Auto switched to GPT-6 Luna, with both new messages and Try Again rejected.

Thanks for the detailed report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332085, which tracks BYOK models missing from the Copilot harness in WSL and other remote workspaces. Your Debian WSL reproduction on 1.145.2 and the comparison showing successful provider registration but no remote BYOK wiring add useful diagnostic evidence to that issue.

Thanks for the report. This duplicates https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/346473, which already includes the fragmented reasoning blocks, broken formatting, and progressive slowdown during longer reasoning responses. We'll consolidate the investigation there.

Thanks for the report. This matches the individual-change Undo failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345575. This report adds Windows and README.md reproduction details on VS Code 1.145.0.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345857, which tracks the same Keep error after forking a chat, along with Undo failures. Your screenshot adds a multi-file occurrence on Windows with VS Code 1.145.0.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345420: changed-file links in a remote Linux workspace open as local files, producing the file-not-found error and backslash paths. Your Copilot CLI session on WSL Debian13 with Code 1.145.0 adds a specific reproduction, including the incorrect file:///home/... URI instead of vscode-remote://wsl+Debian13/....

Thanks for the detailed report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341514, which tracks the same thinking-signature failure and already includes an Amazon Bedrock confirmation. Your Windows 11 / VS Code 1.145.0 reproduction and successful proxy workaround using `anthropic_beta: ["thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01"]` with `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"` add useful Bedrock-specific evidence to that investigation.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is the same bootstrap failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/342764 for tcsh. This report additionally confirms /bin/csh on build a717861c07586a53d83b80d742cd3f59b20a6273 and documents that changing the login shell is not an acceptable workaround in a managed environment; both cases need the bootstrap to run under a compatible shell.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/305853 already tracks exposing conversation identity and an optional request ID to language model providers. This report adds per-chat routing, consistent tier choices, and prompt-cache affinity as concrete use cases for that API.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345420: Copilot's changed-file preview fails for existing remote Linux files with backslash paths, while Source Control diffs work. This report additionally confirms WSL Ubuntu 24.04 on VS Code 1.145.0, with the failure persisting after Reload Window.

Thanks for the report and for checking the workaround. The same Fedora 45 failure when installing any extension is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338194. This thread adds confirmation on VS Code 1.145.0 and two reports that installing `openssl3-libs` restores installation—useful evidence for investigating the package's runtime dependencies.

Thanks for the detailed logs. This matches the remote-path handling tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333447. This report adds macOS, WSL, and Dev Containers confirmations, plus an important distinction: clicking the filename fails, while the adjacent “Open Changes in the Diff Editor” action works as a workaround. Those details should be retained in the consolidated investigation.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This matches the Agent Host account-selection problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340493. This report adds the Claude harness case: its Copilot group is empty despite the preferred work account working in Local, and signing out of the other account restores the models.

Thanks for the detailed report and sanitized logs. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340489 tracks the same Agent Host high CPU and repeated sourceUnresolvable retries, with investigation covering both Claude and Copilot CLI sessions. Consolidating there preserves this report's macOS observations and mixed-provider retry evidence.

Thanks for the detailed feedback. The same concerns about smaller tabs, space around workbench parts, and preserving the classic interface option are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326146. Consolidating there should retain the examples here of indistinguishable tabs with icons disabled, distracting high-contrast separators, and reliance on clear pane boundaries; compact density and connected tabs address parts of that feedback, but do not promise a permanent classic-UI option.

Thanks for the report. This is the workspace-target case of the Windows shortcut-opening problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324353. The detail to retain there is that resolving a `.lnk` targeting a `.code-workspace` file should open the workspace, not the shortcut or workspace JSON as an editor file.

Thanks for the detailed report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327536 already tracks the same missing accessibility semantics on the Markdown editing host. This report adds the explicit requirements for a configurable name defaulting to “Markdown editor” and a stable textbox identity across Editing and Locked modes; those should be included in that work.

Thanks for the report and confirmation. The selection stopping when the pointer leaves the input field is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324675. This report adds confirmation for the Search tab and Find/Replace, including fast drags and movement above or below the fields.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318355 tracks the same problem: another session's approval controls shift the list, so a click intended for Allow can instead mark a session as done. This report adds a macOS occurrence on VS Code 1.131.0 and reinforces the difficulty of finding and restoring the accidentally archived session.

Thanks for providing the logs. They show the local extension host failing to start with `TypeError: Invalid value for env` before the GitHub authentication timeouts. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327815, which tracks the same Windows shortcut-launch failure.

Your report adds the missing authentication output channels and repeated sign-in timeouts, while launching from bash with `--enable-proposed-api vscode.github-authentication` works. These details should be retained with the canonical report; the logs point to extension-host startup rather than establishing that the proposed-API flag is required.

Thanks for the report. This matches the pinned-session disappearance during response generation tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325448. This report adds confirmation on macOS arm64 with VS Code 1.129.0, including that the sessions return when generation completes.

Thanks for the report. The missing Help > Report Issue entry and the issue-template guidance are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317321. This report adds the same behavior on VS Code 1.130.0 / Windows build 22631 with extensions disabled; the question about your `telemetry.feedback.enabled` setting remains relevant to diagnosing it.

Thanks for the report and the additional reproduction through the dynamic launch-configuration gear action. This is the same standalone `launch` configuration policy-validation defect tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/282418; this report adds confirmation that the built-in dynamic configuration flow is affected as well.

Thanks for the detailed report and reproduction. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300484, which tracks automatic RTL/BiDi handling for Copilot Chat responses with mixed English tokens and misplaced punctuation; this report additionally demonstrates the Persian trailing-punctuation case and the `unicode-bidi: plaintext` workaround.

Thanks for the request. This is a task-specific case of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/84072, which tracks showing command arguments in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor. The useful requirement here is to display the task name for `workbench.action.tasks.runTask` bindings and make it searchable, so different task shortcuts can be distinguished without opening JSON.

Thanks for the report. This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/280824: Copilot can finish work without marking the corresponding todos complete. This report adds confirmation that the updates are intermittent on Windows x64 with VS Code 1.128.0.

Thanks for the feedback. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/309223 already tracks reducing stable update frequency and providing slower release channels. This thread also highlights the cost of reconnecting remote and container sessions after update restarts; that feedback belongs in the same discussion.

Thanks for the report. This matches the Issue Reporter preview URL-length failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/247979. Please retain this report's Help > Report Issue > Preview on GitHub reproduction on VS Code 1.128.0 (Windows 10.0.26200) when investigating that issue.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322890, which tracks losing an unsent draft in a new sidebar chat after switching to an existing conversation and returning. Your Windows report also highlights that drafts in ongoing conversations are preserved, unlike drafts in new conversations.

Thanks for the context. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/263129, which tracks showing selected context inline with its file and line range so multiple selections remain distinguishable.

Thanks for the report. The off-center notebook toolbar spinner is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/243027. This report adds that it occurs on Windows with VS Code 1.125.1 and is especially visible at higher magnification, while the individual cell execution spinners rotate normally.

Thanks for the report and the detailed follow-up. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/308616, which tracks agents repeatedly checking terminal output instead of waiting for completion notification. Consolidating there should preserve your Windows/Python example, the Gemini-versus-Claude comparison, and the Gradle report where polling sometimes leads to restarting an unfinished task.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/209653, which also reports that binding notebook.section.runCells to a key does nothing and requests running the active cell's enclosing section. This report adds concrete Windows reproduction steps and identifies the missing fallback when no menu context is supplied.

Thanks for the report. This matches the GitHub sign-in and Copilot authentication timeouts to `4.228.31.149:443` tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316531.

This report adds useful Windows 11 evidence: token exchange succeeds, fetching `https://api.github.com/user` fails through Electron and Node, and curl to the same endpoint succeeds outside VS Code even after the cleanup and firewall checks described above. Consolidating the investigation there does not assume that your network has the same underlying cause.

Thanks for the report and investigation. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/244924, which already tracks macOS Ctrl+F/Ctrl+P cursor movement being cancelled in webview inputs. The reports across multiple extension inputs and the troubleshooting result that no workbench keybinding matched corroborate the webview-host diagnosis. A fix is proposed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/310057, but has not merged; consolidating the reports under the older issue.

Thanks for the detailed Docker Model Runner example. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319968, which requests automatic model discovery for customendpoint providers from a single base URL. Your `http://localhost:12434/engines/v1/models` endpoint and sample response provide a useful concrete case for that work, including displaying the discovered models under the configured provider name.

Thanks for the report. Claude sessions missing a Delete option are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300582. This report adds Windows details for VS Code 1.123.0 and Claude Code 2.1.167, including entries that persist after cleanup in Claude Code; those details belong with the same deletion work.

Thanks for the report and reproduction details. This is the same repeated benchmark-status checking tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/308616. This report adds a concrete async `runtest msbench --benchmark vscbench.say_hello` invocation, reproduction with Opus 4.6 and 4.8, and continued checking even after asking the agent to stop watching; those details remain relevant to the investigation.

Thanks for the detailed report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/294841 already tracks the same Azure-provider rejection of Claude deployments at `/anthropic/v1/messages`, including the need for Messages-protocol support rather than only a hostname change. Consolidating there; this thread adds useful details about protocol selection, authentication headers, deployment-name matching, and the contributor's pending patch and authentication-scope check: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319277#issuecomment-5394159962.

Thanks for the request and the additional detail. The same response-bookmarking capability is already tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/311738; this report adds useful requirements for a visible transcript marker and search/filter access, and confirms that sticky scroll for the latest request is not sufficient.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317863, which remains open for discussion of Copilot inline suggestions suppressing automatic IntelliSense, including TypeScript auto-import suggestions. Your Windows / TypeScript 6.0.3 report adds a clear snooze/re-enable reproduction on VS Code 1.121.0.

To restore automatic IntelliSense without snoozing Copilot, configure:

```json
"editor.quickSuggestions": {
  "other": "on",
  "comments": "off",
  "strings": "off"
}
```
Thanks for the request. Google/Gemini BYOK reasoning-effort configuration is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/315741, so let's consolidate the discussion there.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307481: installing the Azure agent plugin and reloading the window makes it appear uninstalled. This report additionally identifies the same symptom on stable 1.120.0, whereas the earlier report used Insiders.

Thanks for the detailed proposal. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/3553, whose discussion includes Explorer multi-selection, palette/keybinding access, and selection notifications. Let's consolidate there, retaining your three API sketches, the focus-versus-selection and unfocused-state questions, and the additional agent-context use case requesting independent keyboard-focus access.

Thanks for the report. The chat-saving error and stack match https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/315161, which tracks this serialization failure. Consolidating there preserves your additional report of macOS Tahoe 26.4.1 and more than ten crashes in one day; the supplied stack identifies the saving failure but does not establish what caused those crashes.

Thanks for clarifying the request. Local indexing when repository authorization or remote indexing is unavailable is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/294099. This report adds the customer-repository/company-Copilot account mismatch and the workaround of temporarily removing `origin`; those details belong with that fallback request.

Thanks for the report and confirmations. The GHE authentication failure and Auto-only model picker are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/304075. This thread adds the Agents Window reproduction on VS Code 1.120/1.121, the disappearing failed session, and the enterprise sign-in redirect; those details should remain part of the investigation there. The non-GHE report may need separate investigation if it persists independently of enterprise authentication.

Thanks for the report. This matches the auxiliary-window mouse-tracking failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/202410. This report adds a macOS reproduction with VS Code 1.120.0 and extensions disabled: tmux pane resizing works before moving the terminal to a new window, stops afterward, and works again when docked back into the main window.

Thanks for the report and the additional GitHub Spaces example. Explicit MCP OAuth scope selection is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/249663, including authorization failures caused by requesting all advertised scopes. This report adds the concrete requirement to configure scopes for a statically registered client, plus the need to honor explicit scopes with built-in providers when successful but incomplete tool results never trigger step-up authentication; those details should remain part of the scope-selection discussion.

Thanks for the suggestion. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/292921 already tracks sorting Manage Models by its columns, including pricing. Consolidating there, with this report's additional use case of sorting input and output costs independently when a task has a large input but a short answer.

Thanks for the report. This is the same missing Claude Code command already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314660; that report also confirms the error remains after updating VS Code. Your Claude Code 2.1.131 and Windows 10 details are useful additional evidence for that investigation.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314317 already proposes percentage-based feature rollouts and cohort comparisons to catch regressions before wider deployment, covering the staged-release behavior requested here.

Thanks for the report. This is the same Copilot 0.45.1 failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/312374. This report adds that it occurs on VS Code 1.112.0 on Linux when opening VS Code and trying to write a new file.

Thanks for the report. This matches the extension-update failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313714: the same macOS ARM64 Insiders build reports UnknownError with verification not executed across multiple extensions. Your logs add failures for Catppuccin and five other extensions on macOS 25.3.0, plus successful installations of several extensions when verification was skipped; that evidence should be retained in the consolidated investigation.

Thanks for the report. The extension signature-verification failure on Insiders commit 43d0ed45492da1b1ca1738893956de429d46b5e8 is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313714, including logs and multiple macOS confirmations. This report also notes Darwin 24.6.0, severe memory pressure, failure to update VS Code itself, and terminal unresponsiveness as additional diagnostic context.

Thanks for the detailed logs. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313594: both reports show `UnknownError`, `Executed: false` on the same Insiders commit and Darwin arm64 25.4.0. This report adds useful evidence that the failure affects both ESLint and Prettier on an Apple M5 Pro.

Thanks for the report. Auto-mode failures involving expired or invalid session tokens are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300554, where service logs confirm token-expiry errors. This report adds Windows 11 with VS Code 1.119.0-insider and Copilot Chat 0.45.1, two failed-request ID pairs, and the observation that neither debug view showed the errors; those details should remain part of the investigation.

Thanks for the request. COSMIC keyring support is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/239437, which describes the same desktop environment and keyring-detection problem. Consolidating this report there as another request for COSMIC support.

Thanks for the request. The same independent filtering of MCP tool calls and internal Copilot calls is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313198. This report also confirms the request on VS Code 1.118.1, following the upgrade suggestion there.

Thanks for the report and the additional details in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313187. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/292086: clicking a Copilot-changed file in Chat makes the Windows UI slow, while opening the file another way avoids the slowdown. That issue already has paired performance traces. This report adds the VS Code 1.117.0 / Copilot Chat 0.45.1 environment, screen-reader mode enabled, and another user's Windows-only confirmation in the follow-up.

Thanks for the report and workarounds. This matches the older, open report at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/311802: Start Implementation leaves the conversation under Plan-only restrictions instead of enabling implementation.

Consolidating there should retain your Linux Mint/Auto-model reproduction, the model-switch and edit/resend workarounds, and the macOS confirmation linked through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331958, including the failure after manually selecting Agent.

Thanks for the report. This is the same remaining sign-out symptom tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/309667: an authentication modal overlaps the sign-in welcome screen. This report adds that it occurs after completing a session response and then signing out.

Thanks for the detailed request. User-defined folders and groups for Copilot Chat sessions are already requested in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/308516. This report adds useful specifics to that work: a Move to Group context-menu action, collapsible named sections, membership that persists across restarts, and ungrouped sessions remaining at the top.

Thanks for the report and the Ollama-specific confirmation. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/310739, which tracks removed custom models remaining in the model picker because persisted picker/cache state is not cleaned up; the Ollama reproduction and state.vscdb workaround here are useful additional evidence.

Thanks for the report. The overbroad billing-meta redirects are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/291730, where a maintainer has acknowledged that distinct bug reports are being caught by the billing classification. This report adds the model-access example and the concern about misleading Upgrade messaging; the later clarification that Opus 4.5 and 4.6 were removed from Pro+ is important when assessing the underlying behavior.

Thanks for the report. This is the same notebook output toolbar listener warning tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/251838, including the CellOutputElement._attachToolbar → PersistedMenuHideState subscription path. This report adds cross-platform stable-release evidence: approximately 11.3K affected users in 1.116.0 and 10,878 in 1.117.0, with buckets 85812010 and 3f2b8ad6.

Thanks for the report and the Windows confirmation. Changing tools in one session and affecting another running agent is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/296172. Your macOS 1.116.0 report and Windows 1.122.1 confirmation provide additional affected-version details; the question about shared defaults versus running-session isolation belongs with that investigation.

Thanks for the report. The active-file ranking regression is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307605. This report adds useful reproduction details across agent/ask/plan modes on Windows 11, particularly the difficulty finding the active file among identically named Next.js page.tsx files.

Thanks for the detailed report and implementation investigation. The same extension-host `http2` proxy gap is already tracked by the older open issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/185098. Your WSL2 `ENOTFOUND` reproduction and tested `createHttp2Patch` design add useful concrete evidence for that work.

Thanks for the report and confirmation. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/294037: pending questions disappear after switching away from a chat editor tab and back. This thread also confirms the issue on VS Code 1.115.0 and 1.116.0, with closing and reopening the window restoring the dialog; those details remain useful for investigating the shared issue.

Thanks for the report and investigation. The notebook-outline listener warning is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/211105, which includes a large-notebook reproduction and the same per-entry menu subscription stack. This report adds cross-platform telemetry for 1.115.0 and an investigation reporting occurrences across 1.113–1.117; those details belong with the existing issue. The cleanup proposal at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/309157 was closed without merging.

Thanks for the report. Your earlier report at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/308524 covers the same Windows 11 update failure and preserves the complete Code.exe rename error logs, along with the subsequent troubleshooting. Let's consolidate the investigation there.

Thanks for the report and for confirming this still happens on 1.114.0. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307560, which tracks Keep/Undo controls covering suggested code; consolidating there with this report's macOS arm64 details and confirmation after upgrading.

Thanks for the report. The same Git ref-update errors with multiple background windows are tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/303654. This report adds simultaneous failures across all instances when fetching vercel-labs/agent-browser, affecting both origin/main and origin/changeset-release/main; those details should stay with the investigation there.

Thanks for the report and workaround. The delay when entering a complete workspace-relative path is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/131084. VS Code checks relative paths today, but those results still wait for the workspace search; the remaining improvement is to show the exact match without that wait. Your Windows/Samba setup and observation that previously opened files avoid the delay are useful additional evidence for that issue.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/301692, which tracks continuous newline insertion after confirming an Explorer rename with Enter on Fedora/KDE/Wayland. This report also notes that pressing another key stops the insertion; that detail should remain part of the investigation there.

Thanks for the context. The request to turn off the separate Keep/Undo state is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/262495, which Connor linked above. That discussion also includes concerns about older chats affecting newer edits. Your interleaved-session example belongs with that work; `chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay: 1` is a workaround, not removal of the underlying review state.

Thanks for the report. This matches the plan-to-cloud branch-selection problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/296899. This thread adds confirmation on Windows with Copilot Chat 0.40.1, plus the case where dev is the default branch and explicitly requesting main still does not preserve the intended branch.

Thanks for the report and the reload detail. The same missing `tikTokenizerWorker.js` failure on a Remote SSH Linux host is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/291612; this report adds that it occurred on Amazon Linux 2023 and temporarily cleared after reloading Chat.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/302104 tracks both APT update availability and VS Code advertising updates before the package manager offers them, so let's consolidate there. This report adds the Linux Mint 22.3 reproduction and a Debian Trixie observation that repository entries disappear over time; the cause of that deletion remains unconfirmed.

Thanks for the report and the Codespaces details. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297354, which tracks the same user-visible problem: `/memories/session/plan.md` is a virtual memory path but is presented without a reliable link or artifact affordance. This report also confirms that the symptom affects Codespaces and Windows, where the displayed path may resolve as a real but unrelated root-level file.

Thanks for the additional context. This repeats your earlier report at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/298969 with the same versions and environment. Please retain the details there that a simple agent query triggers the error and restarting the window usually restores operation, and confirm whether it still happens after updating VS Code and Copilot.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/57370, which requests that Settings editor modification indicators also identify workspace folders. Your example adds concrete steps using `editor.cursorStyle` and `editor.cursorWidth` in one root’s `.vscode/settings.json`, including the difference between opening that folder directly and opening it within a multi-root workspace.

Thanks for the report and the translation detail. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323072, which tracks the same Chinese-locale status chip obscuring the Problems filter and the underlying shared filter-widget layout. The 页-to-项 correction reported here should be carried into that work.

Thanks for the report. Indexing failing when the Copilot account differs from the GitHub account used to access the workspace repository is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/253359. Consolidating this report there.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This is the same observable multi-window auto-reveal problem tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/200452: the shared Explorer scrolls to another window's active file before the intended Explorer interaction is completed. Your Linux Remote-SSH and directory-click case is useful additional evidence for that issue.

Thanks for the request. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/133198, which tracks messages for skipped tests and their presentation. This report adds the useful requirement that the reason appear on hover without cluttering normal test output.

Thanks for the report and the follow-up reproduction. The Windows crash after confirming Explorer deletion is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/233967. This report adds useful evidence: it reproduces with a temporary user-data directory and extensions disabled, and setting files.enableTrash:false avoids the crash while explorer.confirmDelete remains true. Those details should stay with the Windows investigation; the Linux native-dialog workaround reported later does not establish the same cause.

Thanks for the report. We're tracking code review ignoring `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/280829. This adds the SCM Review Uncommitted Changes case: match `applyTo` against the reviewed files and include instruction files without `applyTo`.

Thanks for the report. This matches the Linux dead-key shortcut regression tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/282752, including the Swiss QWERTZ case previously consolidated from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/283809. This report adds confirmation on Ubuntu 25.10 with VS Code 1.109.5, the recorded [Equal]/circumflex representation, and that switching to the no-dead-keys layout restores the shortcut.

Thanks for the report and logs. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/289879: both fail while initializing chat in a remote environment after selecting the Node fetcher, with api.githubcopilot.com timing out. The additional WSL2 and proxy evidence here is useful for that investigation.

Thanks for the report and the detailed reproduction. The same MCP workspace-variable resolution failure is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/245905. This thread adds a useful Global Install example: the wizard inserts `"cwd": "${workspaceFolder}"`, retaining it when the input is empty, and removing that field allows startup. That detail should remain part of the consolidated investigation.

Thanks for the report. This is the same Claude Opus 4.6 HTTP/2 `stream timeout after 300000` failure already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/296987. This report adds useful WSL2 evidence and an independent confirmation, so the investigation can be consolidated there.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/293849, which tracks inline suggestions replacing modern C# collection expressions with older forms. This report adds a populated-list example (`[1, 2, 3]` becoming `new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 }`) on macOS arm64 with extension 0.37.8.

Thanks for the report. This report adds the Nordic layout on Samsung SM-X710 with Android 13 and Samsung Browser 23: AltGr+2 does not insert @, while AltGr+E successfully inserts €.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/140136 already tracks variable substitution in keybinding command arguments, including `${selectedText}`. Your specific use case—passing the current editor selection to Ctrl+P / Quick Open—belongs in that work too.

Thanks for the report. The same notebook whole-word shortcut failure is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/200295. This report adds an Ubuntu reproduction on VS Code 1.81.1 and 1.82.0-Insiders, including with extensions disabled, and confirms that binding `toggleFindWholeWord` without a when-clause still does not toggle notebook find.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/117656 already tracks the same silent submission failure when the Issue Reporter's authentication session becomes invalid. Consolidating there, with the HTTP 401 / Bad credentials reproduction from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/188169 and the recovery options here: fall back to Preview on GitHub or prompt for re-authentication.

Thanks for the detailed investigation. The same Quick Open behavior is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/101487: file results wait for workspace-symbol search when `search.quickOpen.includeSymbols` is enabled.

This report adds a useful remote OCaml example—13,322 ms for `workspace/symbol` in a roughly 50,000-file workspace—and the suggestion to identify a slow symbol provider while results remain pending. Those details should be retained in the existing discussion. OCaml server-side latency is tracked separately at https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1622.

Thanks for the report. The same GitHub sign-in failure when VS Code runs as administrator is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/164895. This report adds confirmation on VS Code 1.79.0 / Windows build 23475 and the administrator-instance warning; the workaround noted here is to cancel the initial sign-in and accept the alternative login flow.

Thanks for the report and the recent confirmation. This is the same submodule-conflict failure tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/164900: the merge editor cannot apply either submodule revision, leaving the conflict unstaged and the merge blocked. This report additionally confirms the zero-conflict display and inactive commit button through VS Code 1.128.0.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/132921 already tracks identifying settings.json entries whose values match their defaults. Consolidating there; this thread also suggests dimming those entries and offering a bulk-removal code action, with care around defaults changing between versions.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/30191 already includes configurable sizing across all scrollbars and global horizontal/vertical defaults. Consolidating there, with this report's explicit requirement that component-specific settings inherit the global size unless overridden.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. Your Form.Field tooltip sample, selection of the word "field", and additional type="color" example provide useful reproduction details for that issue.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/93470 already tracks distinguishing Explorer-triggered file events from workspace-edit-triggered events, including onWillRenameFiles. Thanks for the request. This report adds a concrete use case worth retaining there: formatting selected Vue HTML with extension.formatSelectionAsHtml, including matching HTML regions with =~ /html/.

Thanks for the request. Touch-drag text selection is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/47770. Your Windows proposal adds a useful interaction option: start horizontally to select or vertically to scroll, then retain that mode even if the drag changes direction. Consolidating there keeps that proposal with the other touch-selection designs.

Thanks for the request. The same native Backspace behavior—removing an indented whitespace-only line and returning to the previous line's end—is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/42785. Consolidating there; this thread also contributes reports that Hungry Delete can disable Backspace until a reload or delay/freeze when suggestions appear, reinforcing the request for native support.

Thanks for the detailed report and sample files. This is the same size-dependent regex Replace All defect tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237975: negated character classes can unexpectedly span newlines on the large-replacement path. This report adds the Windows 10 reproduction with extensions disabled and the specific case where ^([^\t<]+).*$ replaced with $1 clears a following </odstavec> line; those examples should be retained when addressing the shared defect.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/48123, which discusses punctuation ordering in Sort Lines Ascending and includes the same quoted-prefix behavior. This report adds a useful double-quoted JSON example: "abc-def" sorts before "abc", although the unquoted values sort in the opposite order.

Thanks for the request. Extensions can already render gutter icons with `gutterIconPath` and contribute right-click actions through `editor/lineNumber/context`, but those do not provide direct click actions on their decorations. That remaining capability is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/224134, including coexistence with breakpoints and overlapping icons; this thread also contributes the bookmark-click use case and the concern about which decoration receives interaction.

Thanks for the detailed examples. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/27905 already tracks both Ctrl+click whole-word selection and Ctrl+drag selection that snaps to word boundaries. This report adds a useful demonstration (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bfyO8haWKfg) and explains why double-click dragging does not replace the continuous Ctrl-held select-copy-paste workflow; those details remain relevant to that request.

Thanks for the report and the renderer investigation. Inline newline and CR/LF markers are already requested in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/12223, including the expectation that editor.renderControlCharacters should show them. Consolidating there preserves this report's Windows reproduction, the concern about the setting's description, and your source investigation at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/26646#issuecomment-2490997272; this does not mean the capability has been implemented.
